lines.text: Why does popcorn explode into fluffy white clouds when heated, while sweet corn just burns?
Popcorn kernels have an extraordinarily tough, waterproof outer hull called the pericarp.
Inside each kernel sits a tiny droplet of water surrounded by hard, dense starch.
When you heat the kernel past four hundred degrees, that trapped water turns into high-pressure steam.
The steam cooks the dense starch into a molten, gelatinous hot dough.
When internal pressure reaches one hundred and thirty-five pounds per square inch, the hull violently explodes.
As it bursts, the molten starch instantly cools into the delicious crunchy snack you love.
